anisette.title: Anisette servers
anisette.hint: Signing in to Apple needs an anisette server, which tells Apple which computer is signing in. IPAForge uses one that works, by itself; choose one here if you prefer a particular server, or add your own.

modeHint.automatic: Tries the servers in this order and moves on when one fails.
modeHint.none: Pick the server IPAForge should always use.

locked.title: Unlock your device
locked.body: The device is locked, so IPAForge can't talk to it. Unlock it and keep it unlocked until the install finishes.

developer_mode_off.title: Developer Mode is off
developer_mode_off.body: Sideloaded apps need Developer Mode. Turn it on in Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, then restart the device.

not_paired.title: This computer isn't trusted yet
not_paired.body: Unlock the device and tap Trust when it asks whether to trust this computer.

usbmuxd_unavailable.title: Device support isn't running
usbmuxd_unavailable.body: IPAForge can't reach the system service that talks to iPhones and iPads. Install or start it, then try again.

not_found.title: No device found
not_found.body: Connect your iPhone or iPad with a USB cable and unlock it.

disconnected.title: The device was disconnected
disconnected.body: The connection dropped. Reconnect the cable, unlock the device and try again.

pairing_pending.title: Waiting for Trust
pairing_pending.body: Unlock the device and tap Trust on the prompt that appeared.

pairing_denied.title: Trust was declined
pairing_denied.body: The device declined to trust this computer. Pair again and tap Trust this time.

invalid_pair_record.title: The pairing is no longer valid
invalid_pair_record.body: The device no longer accepts this computer's pairing. Unplug it, plug it back in, unlock it and tap Trust.

service_unavailable.title: A device service didn't start
service_unavailable.body: The device refused to start a service IPAForge needs. Unlock it, reconnect it and try again.

protocol_error.title: Unexpected answer from the device
protocol_error.body: The device sent something IPAForge didn't understand. Reconnect it; if it happens again, update IPAForge or report it.

install_failed.title: The install failed
install_failed.body: The device refused to install the app. Try again; if it keeps failing, reinstall the app or report it.

afc_error.title: Couldn't transfer files
afc_error.body: Copying files to the device failed. Unlock it and try again.

timeout.title: The device stopped responding
timeout.body: The device took too long to answer. Unlock it, reconnect it and try again.

passcode_required.title: Set a passcode
passcode_required.body: This needs a device passcode. Set one in Settings › Face ID & Passcode, then try again.

free_app_limit.title: Too many sideloaded apps
free_app_limit.body: A free Apple ID can have only three sideloaded apps active on a device. Remove one, then try again.

profile_banned.title: Apple blocked this Apple ID on the device
profile_banned.body: The device won't accept apps signed with this Apple ID. Retrying won't help: use another Apple ID.

identity_invalid.title: The signing certificate is no longer valid
identity_invalid.body: The device rejected the certificate the app was signed with. Check the computer's clock, or revoke the certificate and try again.

profile_not_found.title: Provisioning profile missing
profile_not_found.body: The device couldn't find the app's provisioning profile. Try again, or reinstall the app.

anisette_unavailable.title: The anisette server isn't responding
anisette_unavailable.body: Signing in to Apple needs an anisette server, and the current one didn't answer. Choose another server or check your network.

anisette_not_provisioned.title: The anisette server isn't ready
anisette_not_provisioned.body: The anisette server couldn't set itself up. Choose another server and try again.

app_id_quota.title: No App IDs left this week
app_id_quota.body: A free Apple ID can register only 10 App IDs every 7 days. Wait for a slot to free up, or use another Apple ID.

certificate_limit.title: Too many certificates
certificate_limit.body: This Apple ID has reached its limit of development certificates. Revoke one, or use another Apple ID.

invalid_credentials.title: Wrong Apple ID or password
invalid_credentials.body: Apple didn't accept the email or password. Check them and enter the password again.

account_locked.title: This Apple ID is locked
account_locked.body: Apple locked this account for security reasons. Unlock it on an Apple device or at Apple's website, or use another Apple ID.

account_refused.title: Apple refused the sign-in
account_refused.body: Apple won't let this Apple ID sign in from here right now. Wait a while, sign in once on an Apple device, or use another Apple ID.

client_rejected.title: Apple rejected the sign-in request
client_rejected.body: Apple didn't accept the identity sent with the sign-in. Choose another anisette server, or wait and try again.

rate_limited.title: Too many requests
rate_limited.body: Apple is limiting requests for now. Wait a few minutes and try again.

service_unavailable.title: Apple's servers are unavailable
service_unavailable.body: Apple's servers didn't respond. Wait a few minutes and check your network.

two_factor_required.title: Enter the verification code
two_factor_required.body: Apple sent a verification code to your trusted devices. Enter it to continue.

two_factor_invalid_code.title: Wrong verification code
two_factor_invalid_code.body: That code didn't work. Check it and enter it again.

two_factor_unsupported.title: This sign-in method isn't supported
two_factor_unsupported.body: This Apple ID uses a two-factor method IPAForge can't handle yet, such as a security key. Use another Apple ID.

sms_unavailable.title: Codes by text message aren't available
sms_unavailable.body: Apple won't send the code by text message here. Get it on a trusted device, or use another Apple ID.

clock_skew.title: The computer's clock is wrong
clock_skew.body: Apple rejects requests when the clock is off. Set the date and time automatically, then try again.

protocol_error.title: Unexpected answer from Apple
protocol_error.body: Apple sent something IPAForge didn't understand. Update IPAForge, or report it if it keeps happening.

session_expired.title: Your session expired
session_expired.body: Sign in to this Apple ID again. If it keeps expiring, check the computer's clock.

account_not_found.title: Apple ID not found
account_not_found.body: IPAForge has no saved session for this Apple ID. Sign in again.

not_eligible.title: This Apple ID can't be used for development
not_eligible.body: Apple doesn't allow this account to sign apps, for example because of its age or terms. Use another Apple ID.

email_unverified.title: Verify your email
email_unverified.body: Apple needs this Apple ID's email address verified first. Verify it, then try again.

team_agreement.title: Accept Apple's agreement
team_agreement.body: The team hasn't accepted Apple's latest developer agreement. Accept it at Apple's developer website, or choose another team.

no_teams.title: No developer team
no_teams.body: This Apple ID has no developer team yet. Accept Apple's developer agreement, or use another Apple ID.

device_limit.title: Device limit reached
device_limit.body: This team can't register any more devices. Choose another team, or use another Apple ID.

app_id_unavailable.title: This App ID is taken
app_id_unavailable.body: Another team already uses this App ID. Choose another team, or use another Apple ID.

invalid_app_id_name.title: Apple rejected the App ID name
invalid_app_id_name.body: Apple didn't accept the name IPAForge chose for the App ID. Update IPAForge, or report it.

certificate_not_revocable.title: This certificate can't be revoked here
certificate_not_revocable.body: Only Apple can revoke this certificate. Revoke a different one instead.

no_devices_for_profile.title: The device isn't registered yet
no_devices_for_profile.body: Apple hasn't finished registering the device. Wait a minute and try again.

developer_request_failed.title: Apple's developer services failed
developer_request_failed.body: A request to Apple's developer services failed. Try again, and report it if it keeps happening.

anisette_server_invalid.title: This anisette server can't be used
anisette_server_invalid.body: Check its name and address: the address starts with https:// or http://.

anisette_server_exists.title: This anisette server is already in the list
anisette_server_exists.body: Choose it from the list in Settings instead.

source_gone.title: The release is no longer available
source_gone.body: The place this app was downloaded from is gone. Choose another channel, import an IPA, or update IPAForge.

unavailable.title: Couldn't load the app list
unavailable.body: IPAForge couldn't fetch the list of apps. Check your network and try again.

download_failed.title: The download failed
download_failed.body: The app couldn't be downloaded. Check your network and try again.

checksum_mismatch.title: The download is damaged
checksum_mismatch.body: The downloaded file doesn't match its checksum, so it wasn't used. Try again or choose another channel.

checksum_missing.title: The download can't be verified
checksum_missing.body: This release has no checksum, so IPAForge can't check it. Choose another channel, or import the IPA yourself.

rate_limited.title: Too many requests to GitHub
rate_limited.body: GitHub is limiting downloads for now. Wait a few minutes and try again.

app_source_unreachable.title: Couldn't reach this source
app_source_unreachable.body: Check the link, and that you're online, then try again.

app_source_invalid.title: This link isn't an app source
app_source_invalid.body: It doesn't list any apps in the AltStore format. Check the link, or add the app's .ipa file instead.

app_source_exists.title: This source is already added
app_source_exists.body: Its apps are in Browse apps already.

invalid.title: The app's settings file is damaged
invalid.body: A property list inside the app couldn't be read. Choose another IPA, or report it.

offline.title: You're offline
offline.body: IPAForge can't reach the internet. Check your network connection and try again.

invalid_macho.title: The app's program is damaged
invalid_macho.body: The app's executable couldn't be read. Choose another IPA.

encrypted_binary.title: The app is encrypted
encrypted_binary.body: This IPA comes from the App Store and is still encrypted, so it can't be re-signed. Choose a decrypted IPA.

unsupported_arch.title: Unsupported app format
unsupported_arch.body: The app's executable uses a format iOS can't run. Choose another IPA.

unsupported_ios.title: Needs a newer iOS
unsupported_ios.body: This app needs a newer iOS version than the device has. Update the device, or choose another channel or IPA.

unsupported_device.title: Not made for this device
unsupported_device.body: This app doesn't support this kind of device, for example an iPad-only app on an iPhone. Choose another IPA.

no_arm64_build.title: No build for iPhone or iPad
no_arm64_build.body: The app has no 64-bit build for iPhone or iPad, for example a 32-bit or simulator build. Choose another IPA.

no_header_space.title: The app can't be signed
no_header_space.body: There's no room in the app's executable for a signature. Choose another IPA, or report it.

zip_slip.title: The IPA is unsafe
zip_slip.body: The IPA tries to write files outside its own folder, so IPAForge refused it. Choose another IPA.

invalid_certificate.title: The certificate is invalid
invalid_certificate.body: The signing certificate couldn't be used. Revoke it so IPAForge can create a new one, then try again.

unknown_issuer.title: Unknown certificate issuer
unknown_issuer.body: IPAForge doesn't recognise who issued the certificate. Update IPAForge and check your network.

invalid_bundle.title: The app bundle is invalid
invalid_bundle.body: The IPA doesn't contain a valid app. Choose another IPA.

invalid_profile.title: The provisioning profile is invalid
invalid_profile.body: The provisioning profile from Apple couldn't be read. Try again, and report it if it keeps happening.

extension_prefix.title: An app extension has the wrong ID
extension_prefix.body: An extension's bundle ID doesn't start with the app's own ID. Choose another IPA.

profile_mismatch.title: The provisioning profile doesn't match
profile_mismatch.body: The profile doesn't match the app it was made for. Try again, and report it if it keeps happening.

profile_expired.title: The provisioning profile expired
profile_expired.body: The profile has expired, or the computer's clock is wrong. Check the clock and try again.

cert_not_in_profile.title: The certificate isn't in the profile
cert_not_in_profile.body: The provisioning profile doesn't include the signing certificate. Try again to get a fresh profile.

device_not_provisioned.title: The device isn't in the profile
device_not_provisioned.body: The provisioning profile doesn't include this device. Try again to get a fresh profile.

step_failed.title: A step failed
step_failed.body: Something went wrong during the install. Try again, and report it if it keeps happening.

prompt_cancelled.title: Cancelled
prompt_cancelled.body: The install stopped because a question was cancelled. Start again when you're ready.

certificate_machine_id_missing.title: The certificate can't be shared
certificate_machine_id_missing.body: This certificate lacks the data SideStore needs to open it. Revoke it so IPAForge can create a new one, then try again.

team_required.title: Choose a team
team_required.body: This Apple ID belongs to several teams. Choose the one to sign with.

kept_ipa_missing.title: This app can't be refreshed here
kept_ipa_missing.body: IPAForge didn't install it on this device, or its kept copy is gone. Add its .ipa in Preload to install it again.

wrong_app.title: This link gives a different app
wrong_app.body: It isn't the app you're refreshing or updating, so it wasn't installed and the app and its data stay as they are. Add the right .ipa in Preload to install it again.

version_unavailable.title: This version can't be downloaded again
version_unavailable.body: Refresh keeps the version on your device, and it's no longer offered for download. Use Update to install the newest version; the app keeps its data.

invalid_message.title: Internal communication error
invalid_message.body: Parts of IPAForge couldn't understand each other. Update IPAForge, or report it.

disconnected.title: Lost connection to the engine
disconnected.body: IPAForge's engine stopped responding. Try again, and report it if it keeps happening.

timeout.title: The engine didn't answer
timeout.body: IPAForge's engine took too long to answer. Try again, and report it if it keeps happening.

aborted.title: Stopped
aborted.body: The operation was stopped before it finished.

unexpected.title: Something went wrong
unexpected.body: An unexpected error happened. Try again, and report it if it keeps happening.

recovery.sign-in-on-apple-device: Sign in on an Apple device
recovery.wait-for-app-id-slot: Wait for a free App ID

switchAccount.title: Use another Apple ID
switchAccount.body: The install starts again with the Apple ID you pick.

waitAndRetry.how: Apple is busy or limiting requests. Wait a minute, then try again.

checkNetwork.how: Make sure this computer is online, then try again.

checkClock.step1: Open the date and time settings on this computer
checkClock.step2: Turn on setting the date and time automatically

reEnterPassword.how: Trying again asks for the password; check it before you enter it.

reEnterCode.how: Trying again asks for a new verification code.

useTrustedDevice.how: When the code is asked for, choose a trusted device instead of a text message.

signInAgain.how: Trying again asks for the password to sign in again.

signInOnAppleDevice.how: Sign in to this Apple ID on an iPhone, iPad or Mac, or at Apple’s website, and follow what it asks:

switchAccount.how: Pick one of your saved Apple IDs. The install starts again with it.

verifyEmail.how: Verify the email address of this Apple ID at Apple’s website:

acceptAgreement.how: Sign in at Apple’s developer website and accept the agreement it shows:

revokeCertificate.how: Trying again asks which certificate to revoke.

waitForAppIdSlot.how: Apple frees each App ID 7 days after it was made. Install again once one is free, or use another Apple ID.
waitForAppIdSlot.next: The next App ID frees on {date}.

chooseAppToRemove.how: Trying again asks which app to remove to make room.

unlockDevice.how: Unlock the device and keep it unlocked until the install finishes.

trustComputer.how: Unlock the device. When it asks whether to trust this computer, tap Trust and enter the passcode.

reconnectDevice.how: Unplug the device, plug it in again and unlock it.

setPasscode.how: Set a passcode on the device in Settings › Face ID & Passcode, then try again.

installDeviceSupport.how: On Windows, install Apple Devices (or iTunes) from Microsoft Store, then restart IPAForge.

reinstallApp.how: Delete the app from the device, then try again.

chooseAnotherChannel.how: The other channel’s build may work on this device.

tryAnyway.how: Apple reported a negative number of App IDs left, which is a known glitch on its side: the real number may be higher. Try anyway asks Apple to create them; if it really is at the limit, it says so.

changeAnisetteServer.how: Open Settings, test the anisette servers, and choose one that works, or go back to Automatic.

recovery.reportHint: Opens a new GitHub issue with the diagnostics filled in. Nothing is sent until you submit it.

revoke.body: This team already has its maximum of development certificates, so IPAForge needs to revoke one to make its own. Apps signed with the revoked one stop refreshing.

share.yesHint: It refreshes your apps on the device by itself
share.noHint: It is installed without your certificate

logs.title: Logs
logs.lede: What IPAForge did, line by line. Open it from anywhere with
logs.cleared: View cleared. Save still writes every line kept this session.
logs.jump: {count, plural, one {# new line} other {# new lines}} · Jump to latest
logs.count: {matching, plural, one {# matching line} other {# matching lines}} · the last {capacity, number} are kept this session
logs.privacy: Passwords, tokens, keys, serial numbers and device identifiers are never written to the logs; they show as [redacted]. Logs stay on this computer until you copy or save them.

none.title: Nothing logged yet
none.body: Lines appear here as IPAForge works: connecting a device, signing in, installing.

noMatch.title: No lines match
noMatch.body: Change the level, the area or the search.

cleared.title: View cleared
cleared.body: New lines appear here as they come.

failed.title: Couldn't read the logs
failed.body: The connection to the Engine may have closed. Reopen Logs to try again.

export.saveTitle: {count, plural, one {Save # line to a file?} other {Save # lines to a file?}}
export.copyBody: The lines shown, with the filters you set.
export.saveBody: Every line kept this session, whatever the filters.
export.warning: Passwords, tokens and device identifiers are already left out, but the logs do name your device model, apps and team. Check them before you post them publicly.

preload.title: Preload apps
preload.description: Install your own apps: signed with your Apple ID, installed over USB, one after another.

catalog.sidestore: Refreshes and installs apps on the device by itself.
catalog.livecontainer: Runs many apps inside one, past the 3-app limit.
catalog.stikdebug: Turns on JIT for apps that need it, on the device.
catalog.feather: Signs and installs apps on the device with your certificate.

browse.title: Browse apps
browse.count: {apps, plural, one {# app} other {# apps}} from {sources, plural, one {# source} other {# sources}}
browse.allOff: Every source is turned off. Turn one on in Sources.
browse.catalogLine: Latest release · checked against its checksum

notRefreshed.title: Couldn't refresh {name}
notRefreshed.body: Showing its apps from the last refresh, {when}.

detail.untrusted: From a source you added: IPAForge doesn't review its apps.
detail.noReleases: Its releases can't be read right now. Check the connection and open it again.

sources.description: Where Browse apps finds apps. Built-in sources are kept by IPAForge; add others by their link (AltStore format).
sources.note: IPAForge doesn't review apps in sources you add. Add only sources you trust.

addSource.title: Add a source
addSource.label: Source link
addSource.hint: A source in the AltStore format, the kind SideStore reads. Usually ends in .json.
addSource.notLink: Enter a link that starts with https://
addSource.notHttps: Use an https:// link: IPAForge only reads sources over a secure connection.
addSource.includes: {count, plural, one {# app, including:} other {# apps, including:}}
addSource.skipped: {count, plural, one {# more left out: its download isn't an .ipa.} other {# more left out: their download isn't an .ipa.}}
addSource.warningBody: IPAForge doesn't review the apps in sources you add. Each app is still checked before it's installed.

removeSource.title: Remove {name}?
removeSource.body: Its apps disappear from Browse apps. Apps installed from it stay on the device, and apps in the To install list stay there too.

list.title: To install
list.empty: No apps yet. Drop .ipa files here, choose them, add a link, or pick one in Browse apps.

row.waiting: Waiting for the device and Apple ID
row.appIds: {count, plural, one {# App ID} other {# App IDs}}{extensions, plural, =0 {} one { (app + # extension)} other { (app + # extensions)}}
row.pairing: Gets the pairing file and certificate

problem.unreadable: IPAForge can't read this file. Add it with Choose files… instead.
problem.needsIos: Needs iOS {needs}; this device has iOS {has}.

summary.appIds: {count, plural, one {# new} other {# new}} · {left, plural, one {# left this week} other {# left this week}}
summary.notEnough: Not enough left. Remove an app, or wait. {next}
summary.freeAppsOver: {used, plural, one {# already there.} other {# already there.}} The install will ask which app to remove, or remove one from this list.

readiness.busy: Wait for the install that's running.
readiness.problems: Remove the apps that can't be installed.

link.title: Add from a link
link.body: A direct link to an .ipa file. IPAForge downloads it, then checks it like any other app.
link.label: Link
link.httpsOnly: Only https links can be downloaded.
link.notIpa: The link must point to an .ipa file.

elsewhere.body: One install at a time: it needs the device. This one can start when it is done.

title.completed: {count, plural, one {{app} is installed} other {# apps are installed}}

run.shared: This device and your Apple ID

refresh.profile: New profile only, nothing installed again
refresh.certificate: Installed again: the certificate that signed it is no longer valid
refresh.unmarked: Installed again: IPAForge can't tell which certificate signed it
refresh.sidestore: Installed again, its data kept, so SideStore itself shows the new date

done.title: {count, plural, one {{app} is on {device}.} other {{app} are on {device}.}}
done.open: Open each app from the Home Screen.

repair.title: Repair SideStore
repair.description: IPAForge checks SideStore on {device} and fixes what keeps it from refreshing your apps by itself.
repair.failedBody: Check that the device is connected and unlocked, then press Check again.

device.title: {device} is ready
device.ok: Unlocked, trusted and with Developer Mode on.
device.locked: It's locked. Unlock it, then press Check again.
device.developerMode: Developer Mode is off, so SideStore and the apps it installs won't open. On the iPhone: Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, then restart it.

signer.title: It's signed with the team you use here
signer.ok: Repair can install it again, or give it a new profile, without losing its data.
signer.otherTeam: Another of this Apple ID's teams signed it. Installing it again with this team would add a second SideStore, without its data or apps.
signer.otherAppleId: Another Apple ID signed it. Installing it again with this one would add a second SideStore, without its data or apps.

version.title: SideStore is up to date
version.outdated: Version {version}; {latest} is out. Older versions can miss fixes for refreshing on recent iOS.
version.unknown: Version {version}. The catalog couldn't be reached to compare.

expiry.title: SideStore hasn't expired
expiry.ok: {days, plural, one {Expires in # day.} other {Expires in # days.}}
expiry.soon: {days, plural, =0 {Expires today.} one {Expires in # day.} other {Expires in # days.}} Once it has expired, SideStore can't refresh itself.
expiry.expired: {days, plural, one {Expired # day ago.} other {Expired # days ago.}} It won't open, so it can't refresh your apps.
expiry.unknown: The device shows no profile for it.

signing.title: The certificate that signed it is valid
signing.revoked: It was revoked or has expired. SideStore stops opening at its next launch.
signing.unknown: Installed by another tool, so IPAForge can't see which certificate signed it. Repair can install it again to be sure.

own.title: SideStore can sign apps by itself
own.ok: It holds a valid certificate to refresh your apps with.
own.missing: It holds no certificate, so its refreshes ask you to sign in, or fail.
own.other: The certificate it was given isn't valid any more. It may have replaced it with a newer one of its own; if refreshing fails in SideStore, install it again.

pairing.title: SideStore has a pairing file
pairing.ok: Present, and this computer's pairing with {device}.
pairing.missing: Missing: SideStore can't reach the device to install or refresh apps.
pairing.other: It's another computer's. It works while that pairing stays valid; resetting Trust on the device breaks it.

manual.title: On your iPhone · IPAForge can't check these

vpn.title: SideStore's VPN is on when it refreshes
vpn.body: Open LocalDevVPN and connect it before refreshing in SideStore.

anisette.title: SideStore can reach its anisette server
anisette.body: In SideStore › Settings › Anisette, pick another server if refreshing says it can't sign in.

plan.title: Repair will
plan.reinstallBody: From the IPAForge catalog, signed with a valid certificate that's also put inside it. Its data and your apps stay.
plan.pairingBody: In SideStore's Documents, replacing what's there.
plan.offerReinstall: Install SideStore again, to be sure
plan.offerPairing: Replace the pairing file with this computer's
plan.hint: One run. Keep {device} connected and unlocked.

blocked.title: SideStore can't be installed again with this Apple ID
blocked.body: Another team or Apple ID signed it, so its data wouldn't carry over. Pick that Apple ID in the top bar, then press Check again.

notInstalled.title: SideStore isn't on {device}
notInstalled.body: Install it first, from the Install page.

fine.title: SideStore is working
fine.body: Nothing to repair. If it still can't refresh, check the two things on your iPhone below.

done.title: SideStore on {device} is repaired.
done.open: Open SideStore and refresh your apps.

remote.title: Remote pairing for iOS 17.4 and later
remote.missing: Missing: SideStore can only use the classic pairing. Placing this computer's pairing file adds it.
remote.rejected: {device} no longer accepts it (its Trust was reset). Placing this computer's pairing file makes a new one.
remote.other: It's another computer's, so IPAForge can't check it. Placing this computer's pairing file replaces it.

sidestore.sourceBody: SideStore shows its apps too, and keeps them up to date on the iPhone. SideStore doesn't review the apps in a source either: add only sources you trust.
sidestore.installBody: SideStore downloads {name} {version}, signs it with your Apple ID and installs it on the iPhone itself. On a free Apple ID it counts toward the 3 apps. It shows in Apps once IPAForge refreshes it.
sidestore.qrLabel: QR code of the link below

steps.camera: Open the Camera on {device} and point it at the code.
steps.banner: Tap the banner to open SideStore.
steps.addSource: SideStore asks to add the source: tap Add.
steps.install: SideStore asks to install the app: tap Install.

sidestore.onPhone: On the iPhone itself, the link opens SideStore too (pasted in Safari, or sent in Messages).
sidestore.offer: {count, plural, one {Add the source you added here to SideStore too, so it shows its apps on the iPhone.} other {Add the # sources you added here to SideStore too, so it shows their apps on the iPhone.}}

checklist.title: On {device} · iOS {ios}
checklist.progress: {left, plural, one {# thing to do} other {# things to do}} · {done} of {total} done

cable.title: Connect {device} to this computer
cable.how: Use a cable the first time; after that, Wi-Fi works while both are on the same network.

unlock.title: Unlock it
unlock.how: Keep it unlocked while IPAForge installs.

trust.title: Trust this computer
trust.step2: Tap Trust when it asks about this computer.

passcode.title: Set a passcode
passcode.how: SideStore refreshes over Wi-Fi, which iOS only allows with a passcode: Settings › Face ID & Passcode.

devmode.title: Turn on Developer Mode
devmode.step1: Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode (if it isn't there, press Show the option).
devmode.step3: After the restart, tap Turn On and enter the passcode.
devmode.revealed: It's in Settings › Privacy & Security now.

developer.title: Trust your Apple ID as a developer
developer.step3: Tap Trust. The iPhone needs the internet for this.

vpn.title: Install LocalDevVPN
vpn.how: SideStore talks to the iPhone through this local VPN; nothing leaves the phone. It's free on the App Store.
vpn.qrLabel: QR code of LocalDevVPN's App Store page
vpn.scan: Scan with the Camera, or search "LocalDevVPN" in the App Store.

vpnOn.title: Connect LocalDevVPN when SideStore refreshes
vpnOn.how: Open LocalDevVPN and tap Connect, or let SideStore turn it on: it asks the first time.

repair.title: SideStore can refresh by itself
repair.how: Its certificate, its pairing file and its expiry.

checklist.notice: {count, plural, one {# thing to do on {device}} other {# things to do on {device}}}
checklist.noticeBody: So installing and refreshing go smoothly.

downloading.title: Updating IPAForge
downloading.body: Version {version} is out. It downloads and installs now, then IPAForge opens again by itself.

installing.title: Installing {version}…
installing.body: IPAForge opens again in a moment.

failed.title: The update didn't finish
failed.body: Version {version} is out. Try again, or download it from its release page.

manual.title: IPAForge {version} is out
manual.body: This copy was installed from {package, select, msi {a .msi installer} deb {a .deb package} rpm {an .rpm package} other {a package}}, which can't update itself. Download the new version and install it over this one: your Apple IDs, apps and settings stay.

nativeBuild.title: This is the Intel build
nativeBuild.body: Your Mac has Apple silicon, so this copy of IPAForge runs through Rosetta and everything is slower. Download the Apple silicon build and install it over this one; your Apple IDs, devices and apps stay.

page.title: What's new
page.lede: Everything that changed in IPAForge, newest first.

portal.description: What your Apple ID’s team holds at Apple, and the profiles on your device.

noAccount.title: No Apple ID yet
noAccount.body: Sign in with an Apple ID on Accounts to see what its team holds.

certificates.hint: A certificate signs the apps you install. Revoking one stops every app it signed from opening, until they’re signed again.
certificates.empty: The team has no certificates yet. IPAForge makes one the first time it installs.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke this certificate?
revokeDialog.apps: These stop opening on {device} until they’re signed again (Refresh on Apps does it):
revokeDialog.none: Nothing on {device} is signed with it.
revokeDialog.noDevice: Connect your device to see which of its apps this certificate signs.
revokeDialog.thisComputer: IPAForge makes a new one the next time it installs or refreshes.
revokeDialog.sidestore: SideStore made it to refresh by itself: it makes a new one the next time you sign in there.
revokeDialog.machine: Xcode on that computer makes a new one the next time it signs.

appIds.hintFree: Each app and extension you install needs one. Free teams can register 10 in 7 days; each counts for 7 days after it’s made.
appIds.hintPaid: Each app and extension you install needs one. Paid teams have no weekly limit.
appIds.left: {count, plural, one {# left this week} other {# left this week}}
appIds.empty: The team has no App IDs yet.

deleteDialog.title: Delete this App ID?
deleteDialog.free: On a free team it still counts against the 10 a week until it expires: deleting it doesn’t give the slot back sooner.
deleteDialog.paid: It can be registered again later.

profiles.title: Provisioning profiles on {device}
profiles.hint: A profile lets one app (or extension) run on this device. Refresh gives an app a new one; an expired or unused one is safe to remove.
profiles.noDevice: Connect your device to see its provisioning profiles.
profiles.empty: There are no provisioning profiles on this device.

removeDialog.title: {count, plural, one {Remove this profile?} other {Remove # profiles?}}
removeDialog.body: {count, plural, one {It’s removed from {device}. No app there needs it.} other {They’re removed from {device}. No app there needs them.}}

groups.hint: Apps in the same group share files (SideStore and its widget, for example). IPAForge makes them when an app needs one.
groups.empty: The team has no app groups yet.

devices.hintFree: Apps you sign run only on these.
devices.hintPaid: Apps you sign run only on these. Paid teams can register 100 a year; removing one is done on Apple’s developer site, once a year.
devices.empty: No devices are registered yet. IPAForge registers yours the first time it installs.
